# Nisco and MLILY Supreme frozen literals

These fixtures preserve the accepted app reports' static derivations, not
hardware captures. Nisco 1.1.1 (code 3) has 396 vector records; MLILY Supreme
1.3.1 (code 5) has 399 original vectors and 25 separate diagnostic repair cases.
Counts overlap wire, parser and parameter domains, and are not feature counts.

The artifacts came from the frozen 2026-07-14 delivery. Hardware is unverified;
there is no fresh latest-version claim. `richmat_cluster022_proof.py` checks
production builders against outbound literals before choosing a runtime.

The Nisco five-case repair records current dispatch mode, including a mode
switch after scheduling. MLILY diagnostic cases retain exact capability/start/
stop precedence, nibble fields, guarded append behavior and generic INIT fallback.
The malformed generic LONG-worker example remains separate from the finalized
fixed-remote save caller. Nisco's current UI attachment is NOT_ESTABLISHED;
MLILY's absence of an attached current RvText longCode is independently accepted.
The raw worker is not implementation-tested or treated as a hardware capture.
